approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It keeps the highest-scoring survivors, favors their upper score bands when choosing parents, and generates offspring with mutation chains and connected-fragment crossover. Accepted offspring can become later parents. Every accepted score also enters a complete archive used by a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to select each evaluation batch from a larger fresh candidate pool through correlated posterior draws. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while ordinary graph edits, stable molecular identity checks, duplicate rejection and bounded fallbacks remain active.
approach.novelty: Test one registered combination linking survivor retention to its breeding consumer: keep the incumbent and newest other live records, then draw parents uniformly from every eligible live survivor. The recency-only sibling stored extra records that never bred; the uniform-live sibling used otherwise unsupported parents under greedy retention. Both lowered the mean. This exact joint implementation supplies the missing fourth treatment, follows protected records into actual use and scored descendants, and measures the total interaction. It differs from recent-score-tie priority and core-based retention, and makes no separate component-benefit or performance-rescue claim.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-62daf219c70a retains the highest-scoring live records and samples only its upper score bands; at capacity its unexcluded breeding support covers ranks 0 through 31 of 64 survivors. Its complete current-profile mean is 0.5956696497334577 with seed population SD 0.02659287062806747, verified against all three original summary.json and run.log files. The limiting behavior for this question is storage without delivery to the breeding consumer. The exact recency-only child n-8fa256ded991 changes 3483 of 3540 capacity-contested sets and directly protects 135 distinct records, 124 of which occur in later live states, but none subsequently gains sampling support or breeds. Shared-survivor rank/probability changes do reach accepted offspring, so that total contrast is exposed; its mean is 0.583862951276973, down 0.011806698456484669. The exact uniform-live-only child n-a56491c332aa makes 53199 actual draws from previously unsupported ranks and those parents participate in 1427 evaluated products, but its mean is 0.5496716372958006, down 0.04599801243765703. These are adverse individual results, not evidence of a performance rescue. The same-Parent recent-tie child n-03acfe1ba8af leaves all 145 cutoff-protected records unused and loses 0.020778516441214645; the older core-round child n-28dc36ed5be7 in c-2c9141d5f8 leaves 602 protected records unused under a different Parent/profile and also loses. The missing evidence is whether the exact recency rule plus its all-live consumer delivers directly protected records to actual scored descendants and what the complete four-treatment interaction is. Source diffs and all nine original Anchor/recency/uniform search receipts establish the two sources share one code Parent and epoch-1 profile; the new joint outcome remains unobserved.
hypothesis: Jointly replace nonincumbent greedy survivor membership with the exact incumbent-preserving newest-serial rule from n-8fa256ded991 and replace rank-preferred live-parent choice with the exact all-eligible-live uniform law from n-a56491c332aa, on the single code Parent n-62daf219c70a, to connect directly protected survivors to their breeding consumer.

finding_summary.headline: Protected records reached scored offspring, but the joint mean fell and the interaction was negative
finding_summary.insights:
Changing the consumer removed the storage-without-use obstruction observed with recency alone, but making protected alternatives breed did not recover endpoint performance. This is a resolved negative result for the exact joint intervention and its matched-panel interaction. It does not assign the loss to either component separately or settle the value of the wider graph-evolution foundation. The original losses from both single controls remain.

Participation and productive search separated sharply: the joint run produced 1,060 strict generating-parent wins versus 629 for the Parent, against weaker generating parents, while sequential incumbent advances fell from 258 to 201. Protected ancestry reached 525 accepted records and twelve incumbent advances, but only one final leader; overlapping ancestry is not proof that a retained structure mediated the endpoint. More perceived molecular cores likewise did not establish useful chemical diversity: the molecular assessment found 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic cores versus 1,850 and 1,117 for the Parent, alongside 299 tiny products versus 99 and continuing unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. Recognizable cyclic amines and carbonyl frameworks remain counterexamples to treating every product as implausible. Neither core counts nor founder reachability measures retained atoms or synthetic feasibility.

The fixed combination has an exposed, complete answer without rescue tuning. Why particular trajectories lose, which chemistry would be useful, and how the broader foundation contributes remain open; this shared-Parent panel supplies neither independent replication nor reliability beyond the issued seeds.
finding_summary.results:
The access mechanism worked. Of 196 records retained against a local greedy eviction, 182 reached a later live population and all 182 were subsequently sampled, in 3,736 parent draws. The other 14 had no later opportunity. Those parents produced 155 accepted offspring, of which 151 later bred. Only two immediately advanced the incumbent. The stricter group still directly protected at the consumed retention contest produced 61 accepted offspring and no immediate incumbent gains. In median_2 seed 2, protected parents were drawn 140 times but produced no accepted offspring. All fifteen joint task runs completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.530508, a paired loss of 0.065161. All three seed macros and all five task means declined; three of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. The joint mean was also 0.053355 below recency alone and 0.019163 below uniform-live sampling alone. The four-treatment interaction, joint minus recency minus uniform plus the Parent, was −0.007357, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its seed values were +0.025676, −0.057736 and +0.009990, with population deviation 0.036194, so the negative mean does not describe every seed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and aryl-amine families persist, alongside more tiny fragments, unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character:
All supplied Child and published Parent trajectories were read for all five objectives and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all seeds matched and no profile mismatches. The indexed published recency-only n-8fa256ded991 and uniform-live-only n-a56491c332aa trajectories were also read descriptively: 60 files and 18,000 observations in total, with no missing paths. Each node contributes 4,500 observations, including 4,350 optimizer products and 150 fixed initial records; each task contributes 870 optimizer products. No task was omitted. Only accepted evaluated products and initial observations are visible in these trajectories; unselected candidate pools have no invented scores or inferred chemistry coverage. The digest final_molecules are the tail of seed 2, not every seed's best molecule. All seed leaders and selected low and final examples below come from the full trajectories. Original indexed molecular reports for the Parent and both component comparators were read to preserve the source and conditions of recurring gaps.

The Child produces recognizable annulated aryl carboxamides and ketones, azaarene/carbonyl assemblies, biaryl cyclic amines, cyclic urea/imide-like systems, fluorinated carbocycles and thiourea/hydrazone structures. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts, in fixed task order, are 24, 34, 32, 31 and 26, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Across the Child, the range is one to 113 heavy atoms and the median is 28 heavy atoms with four RDKit-perceived rings. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: digest ring-digit incidences range from 0.8621 to 0.9517, and aromatic-text incidences from 0.6425 to 0.9253. These are the fraction of molecule strings containing the feature, not the fraction of atoms aromatic, physical ring feasibility or scaffold counts. The chemically recognizable families and conventional cyclic-amine leaders are meaningful counterexamples to calling every output implausible. Nevertheless, reactive-looking local bonds, constrained unsaturation, complex bridges and many unspecified configurations justify questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality; none is a synthesis or activity measurement.

The distinction between identities, perceived cores and ancestry matters. Over the evaluated optimizer records the Child has 4,138 distinct exact SMILES and 2,005 nonempty typed / 1,327 generic Murcko cores; Parent has 4,286 strings and 1,850 / 1,117 cores. The component comparators have 1,782 / 1,055 and 2,060 / 1,403 cores, respectively. Generic cores replace atom types and bond orders, and all core counting omits stereochemistry; empty acyclic cores are excluded. This shows substantial perceived topology variation, while recurring leading families within seeds support moderate rather than collapsed chemical diversity. It does not show independent plausible pharmacophores, useful diversity or atoms retained from a founder. Trajectory files do not map atoms or provide actual-parent ancestry; founder reachability, if supplied by a separate provenance audit, remains graph ancestry rather than conserved scaffold chemistry. No protected-record, component-activation or chemical-mediation conclusion is drawn here.

The Child includes 299 products with at most three heavy atoms, versus Parent 99, recency-only 105 and uniform-live-only 134; 425 Child products are acyclic versus Parent 129. Conversely, direct N-halogen / O-halogen / O-O bond-bearing record counts are 489 / 145 / 114 for Child, 1,042 / 278 / 273 for Parent, 897 / 456 / 319 for recency-only and 483 / 247 / 157 for uniform-live-only. These overlapping counts are whole-record occurrences, not distinct bonds or a combined quality score. Ring-triple-bond and ring-cumulated-carbon flags occur in 41 and 61 Child products, versus 17 and 42 in Parent. Fewer heteroatom-halogen flags therefore do not establish general chemical improvement. RDKit identifies possible unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,446 Child products versus 2,408 Parent products, while all Child digest stereocentre and charge-string incidences are zero. Neutral tertiary amines remain plainly present, so absence of charge notation does not mean absence of basic sites. Potential centres are structural flags, not proof of configurational stability.

The per-seed endpoint scores below are existing trajectory observations, not newly assigned scores. Their structural associations do not identify why a score changed, the objective's full desired chemistry, or separate effects of the two jointly changed decisions. The current comparison has one code Parent, and the published component trajectories remain their own adaptive histories. No additive chemical contribution, significance, unseen-seed reliability or whole-foundation value follows. Read-only CPU descriptor definitions, original trajectory hashes and all records are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot3-molecular/trajectory_descriptors.json and molecule_records.jsonl; describe.py reproduces them without candidate or oracle execution.

The earlier n-c55c3d520a2c source provenance is historical: its profile boundary is not converted into a matched comparison here. Current complete pairing refers specifically to n-62daf219c70a.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 evaluated optimizer products range from one to 39 heavy atoms, median 24, with median three perceived rings. Ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.8897 and 0.8678. All three seed leaders have 25 heavy atoms but different local ring chemistry. Seed 0 evaluation 291, score 0.42762099872850584, is a methoxy/methyl arene fused to a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring, with an amino-bearing saturated centre and an N-fluoro aryl carboxamide. Seed 1 evaluation 190, 0.4163503402962837, carries a fused seven-membered N-N ring, a carbon-bound chloride, hydroxymethyl group and fluoropyridyl ketone; it has no N-halogen bond. Seed 2 evaluation 299, 0.45555627303128626, is an ethynyl/methoxy/methyl N-methyl indole-like carboxamide whose amide nitrogen bears fluorine and a pyridyl substituent. The observed makeability ranges from recognizable aromatic amide chemistry to unusual nitrogen substitution and uncertain cyclic geometry. The seed-2 evaluation-253 benzofuran-like N-methyl pyridyl carboxamide, 0.4272212457957658, is a relatively conventional counterexample with carbon-bound fluorine and no direct N/O-halogen or peroxide bond.
liabilities: N-F carboxamides occur in the seed-0 and seed-2 leaders; N-hydroxy and N-N alternatives require their own stability and synthetic assessment rather than being treated as automatically ordinary.
A seed-1 near-leader at evaluation 278 scores 0.41605207864642335 despite cyclic cumulated double bonds. High score and a parseable SMILES do not establish feasible ring geometry.
There are 72 products with at most three heavy atoms, and late tiny proposals coexist with developed multiring structures.
missing_features: The leading set does not consistently combine its useful aromatic-carbonyl organization with ordinary amide nitrogen substitution and credible ring geometry. Such alternatives are partially present, including the benzofuran-like tertiary amide, so this is incomplete coverage rather than an inability to make aromatic rings or amides.

Configuration is unspecified at saturated ring centres in the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders. These trajectories contain no matched stereoisomer comparison and do not establish that specifying one would improve the score.
No unique missing target motif can be inferred from these records: both fused aromatic and partially reduced N-ring series reach the upper observed range.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole aryl amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. Higher examples retain an organized aromatic/polar carbonyl framework while altering methoxy content, side chains, ring constitution and nitrogen environment. The score does not require N-F: the seed-1 leader lacks it, and the seed-2 N-hydroxy carboxamide at evaluation 262 scores 0.44989726212142783. Late fragmentation remains costly: seed-2 evaluation 298, OCF, scores 8.28920643387263e-20, while evaluated elemental or tiny unsaturated fragments reach zero. These comparisons support molecular context rather than an isolated functional-group prescription. Parent leaders for seeds 0/1/2 score 0.39405142067435733 / 0.47411701813450596 / 0.438972502037081 and remain substituted fused aromatic N systems with N-halogen groups. The Child therefore has both higher and lower seed endpoints, without a consistent gain from a particular ring or halogen change. The component-comparator leaders also preserve carbonyl/aromatic families, including halogen-free examples and larger or spiro ring variants; neither explains the joint output by itself.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated set ranges from one to 113 heavy atoms, median 34, with median four perceived rings; ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.8621 and 0.8425. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 299 scores 0.6034633506581824 and contains 45 heavy atoms: linked pyrazole/aryl/azaaryl regions, substituted urea and formamide carbonyls, conjugated imino functionality, halogens, and a triple bond in a six-membered oxygen-containing ring. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 295 scores 0.5990766677041187 and contains 38 heavy atoms, with an imino aryl group, linked or annulated N heterocycles, carbonyl/ester side chains and direct O-F. The terminal seed-2 leader at evaluation 300 scores 0.6115618661257607 and has 49 heavy atoms, six perceived rings, azaaromatic/nitrile and cyclic-carbonyl regions, methoxy/acetal substituents and O-Cl. This is bulky, largely aromatic and heteroatom-rich output with serious local bond and geometry questions. Recognizable carbonyl and azaarene components do not by themselves make the assembled structures synthetically persuasive.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader contains a cyclic triple bond despite aromatic labels. The task set contains 41 ring-triple-bond-bearing products; graph perception does not validate their geometry.
Direct O-F and O-Cl in the other seed leaders raise context-dependent reactivity and makeability concerns. They are distinct from carbon-bound aromatic fluorine or chloride.

Large appended or coupled modules, flexible oxygenated side chains and imino groups add complexity without proving useful functional organization; 70 products are at most three heavy atoms at the other extreme.
The seed-2 best is terminal. Its structure and observed score say nothing about later descendants or retained atom provenance.
missing_features: The observed Child leaders do not demonstrate the compact, strongly scoring heteroatom/carbonyl organization seen in the Parent seed-0 leader. This is an observed coverage difference, not a prescription to reproduce that molecule or its reactive bonds.

Credible alternatives to constrained cyclic triple bonds and direct O-halogen substitution are not consistently combined with the upper observed scores. Near-scoring alternatives lacking those particular bonds do exist, and may retain other liabilities.
No unique rewarded scaffold can be identified from the trajectories; decorated size and ring count are inadequate proxies for the favorable connected arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best, evaluation 7, scores 0.548381482770623. Very small optimizer products such as seed-0 evaluation 48, dimethyl ether, score 0.5. The 37-heavy-atom seed-2 evaluation-69 sulfone/polyene/carbonyl-N assembly scores 0.2888457269700333, showing that size and aromatic complexity alone are insufficient. The seed-2 43-heavy-atom nitrile/carbonyl-thione alternative at evaluation 272 scores 0.6023391812865497 without O-Cl, and seed-1 evaluation 296 scores 0.5923490233391169 with an O-formyl group instead of O-F but also other structural differences; neither is a controlled single-bond replacement. The visible gradient is consistent with particular connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements, not simply more rings or more halogen. Parent seed leaders score 0.8561477222467935 / 0.6248206599713055 / 0.6178024026512013. Its strongest leader has 30 heavy atoms and compact fused N/carbonyl/thione and azaaryl chemistry, but also O-F and a chloromethyl ether; the Child's larger leaders do not reproduce its upper score range. Recency-only leaders span 0.6030158256195879 to 0.6431665876937657 and uniform-live-only leaders 0.5983092961702587 to 0.6077243572172578, with their own hypohalite, peroxide, nitrogen and ring liabilities. These are comparator chemistries, not evidence that either component supplied or removed a required fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The products range from one to 90 heavy atoms, median 32, with median three rings and two aromatic rings; ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.9437 and 0.9253. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 242, score 0.9999886694484911, is a 26-heavy-atom N-propyl azetidine linked through an alkyl chain to a fluorinated/methylated biphenyl with a fluoromethyl substituent. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 293, 0.9636142513873031, is a 27-heavy-atom substituted N-methyl pyrrolidine joining two fluorinated aromatic regions, with a methoxy-bearing benzylic centre and phenol. Both contain recognizable basic aliphatic amines and carbon-bound fluorine without the flagged N/O-halogen or peroxide bonds. Seed 1 diverges: evaluation 295, 0.7437807598425547, is a 30-heavy-atom halogenated diaryl cyclohexene with a methoxy-thiol-type O-CH2-SH substituent and no nitrogen atom. Its crowded substituted carbon ring and sulfur terminus warrant more scrutiny than the simpler cyclic-amine series. Plausible medicinal-chemistry motifs therefore exist, but the whole output is neither uniform nor uniformly persuasive.
liabilities: The leading aryl-amine structures are heavily hydrophobic and halogenated by inspection, with uncertain balance of polar and nonpolar groups; no measured solubility, exposure or biological activity is supplied.
Seed-1 evaluation 263 and its final product contain acid chloride functionality, and the leader retains an unusual oxygen/sulfur terminus. High score does not certify stability or synthesis.
RDKit detects possible unassigned centres in 807 of 870 optimizer records. Ordinary azetidines and pyrrolidines are counterexamples to any blanket objection to small saturated N rings.
missing_features: The seed-1 leading series lacks the available aliphatic amine-and-aromatic organization repeatedly present in the higher-scoring seed-0, seed-2 and Parent leaders. The generator already makes such amines elsewhere, and nitrogen-containing seed-1 relatives show that merely adding nitrogen is not sufficient.
The cyclic-amine leaders leave stereochemical relationships at substituted saturated and benzylic centres unspecified; no enantiomer or diastereomer preference can be inferred.
The score record supplies no protonation or binding-pose information. Zero charge-string incidence cannot be interpreted as a lack of protonatable chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.01904115112334333. Very low optimizer products include seed-0 evaluation 25, an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ester at 0.00016747245492913543, and seed-1 evaluation 33, a sulfonamide-bearing pyrrolidine/amide-acid fragment at 0.0006926945710016989. In contrast, the seed-0 and seed-2 upper range accompanies a nonacylated cyclic tertiary amine positioned between or near hydrophobic aromatic regions. This is a repeated association, not a measured binding mode or proof that an amine is sufficient: seed 1's nitrogen-free leader is well above its early lows, its nitrogen-containing acid-chloride relative at evaluation 263 scores 0.731564594156626, and the seed-2 final sulfur/amine-rich product scores 0.3544714456182126. Parent leaders score 0.9999989177995104 / 0.9969753164881906 / 0.9999934235240012 and all retain available aliphatic amines on flexible, cyclic or fused aryl arrangements. The corresponding recency-only leaders also retain aryl/amine combinations; the uniform-live-only seed-0 leader is an ordinary biaryl azetidine, while its other leaders are more complex ring systems. The Child seed-1 absence of a basic nitrogen among its leading constitution is a descriptive chemical difference, not proof that either retention or sampling caused its lower endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated products range from one to 71 heavy atoms, median 31, with median five perceived rings and two aromatic rings; ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.9517 and 0.9253. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 233, score 0.18867027068276818, is a 23-heavy-atom annulated aromatic N system connected to a nine-membered N-alkyl dicarbonyl ring. Seed 1 evaluation 175, 0.18753249934291275, has 33 heavy atoms and six perceived rings: a quinoline-like aromatic ether region connected to a densely bridged amine/lactam/urea-like cage with an acetyl group. Seed 2 evaluation 241, 0.21177936240075523, has 27 heavy atoms, alkyl substituents, an aromatic-labelled N-containing annulated system and a cyclic N-methyl dicarbonyl group; RDKit perceives rings of sizes six, seven and nine. The enlarged aromatic-labelled ring is a geometry/aromaticity question rather than proof of a conventional aromatic scaffold. All three leaders are free of direct N/O-halogen and O-O bonds. Their local carbonyl/amine chemistry is recognizable, but the medium-ring and cage connectivities leave synthetic plausibility uncertain.
liabilities: Medium rings, cross-links and dense ring junctions complicate conformational and synthetic interpretation. The seed-2 nine-membered aromatic-labelled N ring deserves explicit scrutiny.
The 51-heavy-atom terminal coupled product has duplicated carbonyl/N-rich regions and is worse-scoring than the compact leader; larger size is not evidence of useful chemical coverage.
The leading examples demonstrate that direct heteroatom-halogen bonds are not necessary for the upper observed scores here, although such bonds occur elsewhere in the evaluated set.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently recover the upper observed aromatic/carbonyl/amine organization of the Parent across its seeds. These features themselves are present; their productive arrangement and alternatives are the coverage gap.
The cage and enlarged-ring families lack independent geometric or synthetic support. Straightforward functional groups embedded in a parseable graph do not establish a feasible complete molecule.
The seed-1 cage leaves its potentially stereogenic junctions unspecified; the trajectories cannot assign a score penalty to that omission.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused N-dicarbonyl/arene molecule at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329. The upper range retains combined aromatic and carbonyl/nitrogen organization; it is only modestly separated from this initial example. Tiny proposals including seed-0 evaluation 265, water, and seed-1 evaluation 197, hydrazine, score zero. More elaboration is not uniformly favorable: the seed-2 final 51-heavy-atom coupled assembly scores 0.15510900536560693, below its 27-heavy-atom leader. Replacing a leader carbonyl environment by an imino environment in seed-2 evaluation 274 gives 0.20115274729832738; this illustrates tolerated local variation without proving a unique required group. Parent leaders score 0.2258403994203931 / 0.2214095461892601 / 0.22600312875247064, and retain alkylated aromatic N systems linked to cyclic carbonyl/amine frameworks at 34, 32 and 29 heavy atoms. Recency-only leaders occupy related medium-ring aromatic/carbonyl families; uniform-live-only leaders also include enlarged or caged variants. All three Child endpoints are lower than their matched Parent observations despite many perceived cores. The record supports sensitivity to connectivity and functional-group arrangement, not ring abundance alone.

per_task.generated_character: The products range from one to 50 heavy atoms, median 26, with median four perceived rings but only one aromatic ring. Ring-digit incidence is 0.8644 and aromatic-text incidence 0.6425, so this set is substantially less uniformly aromatic than the other tasks; it is not ring-poor. Seed 0 evaluation 194, score 0.49469115575536243, is a 28-heavy-atom N-rich fused dione with a fluorinated cyclopropyl group and fluoroethyl substituent, including a constrained fused four-membered connection. Seed 1 evaluation 188, 0.4987766923969328, is a 25-heavy-atom wholly nonaromatic thiourea/hydrazone-like assembly with a partially unsaturated hydroxy carbocycle, a fluorohydroxy cyclopropene and a fluorinated small imine-containing N ring. Seed 2 evaluation 280, 0.5551603988142229, is a 25-heavy-atom bridged or annulated amino carbocycle/N-dicarbonyl system with carbon-bound fluorine and two N-F bonds; the perceived ring sizes are five, seven, seven and eight. This is distinct seed chemistry rather than a single aromatic family, but the constrained unsaturation, unusual N bonds and stereochemical omissions make the leaders questionable synthesis targets.
liabilities: The seed-2 leader has two N-F bonds, while seed-0 and seed-1 leaders instead expose small constrained ring connections or unsaturation. Removing one bond flag alone would not resolve all chemistry concerns.

There are 43 molecules with a ring carbon carrying two double bonds, and the supplied cumulated-double-bond string incidence is 0.0552; these different graph and text definitions must not be conflated.

The set includes 86 products with at most three heavy atoms, and 573 products with possible unassigned tetrahedral centres. Neither a high ring count nor RDKit parsing establishes stability, stereochemical identity or synthesis.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently reach the higher observed compact fluorinated polar-group arrangements of the Parent, but fluorination, carbonyls, amines and N heterocycles are already available. The records do not identify a unique missing group.

Plausible ring geometry is not consistently combined with the favored local polar/fluorinated environments. Carbon-bound fluorine without N-F is present in strong examples, so direct N-fluorination cannot be treated as a chemical necessity.
The multiple fluorinated ring centres and junctions lack stereochemical specification, and no matched stereoisomer or molecular-state comparison is available.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best, evaluation 7, scores 0.0020944534688323298; the shared initial thiourea/hydrazone example at evaluation 3 is only 4.620656635650526e-15. The upper observed range accompanies compact fluorinated N/O/S-containing ring frameworks rather than isolated halogens or unrestricted molecular growth. Seed-1 evaluation 153, F, scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, while the seed-0 50-heavy-atom doubled carbonyl/N-ring assembly at evaluation 56 scores 2.1720424118142743e-25. Seed-0's final four-heavy-atom unsaturated oxygen ring scores 5.554325974994788e-20. Aromaticity and N-F are not universal requirements: the seed-1 leader has no perceived aromatic ring and neither seed-0 nor seed-1 leader has N-F. Parent leaders score 0.6510211907030741 / 0.4870057305679067 / 0.7208853668418119 and are fluorinated imino/carbonyl N systems; the strongest Parent example lacks N-F but contains problematic cyclic cumulation and an enlarged aromatic-labelled ring. The Child seed-1 observation is higher than its Parent, while the other two are lower. Recency-only leaders retain fluorinated imino/carbonyl families; uniform-live-only includes a carbon-bound-fluorinated dione without N-F at 0.6054403589897509 and an N-fluorinated thiourea/hydrazone at 0.4438102388357315. These mixed counterexamples prevent a target motif or aromaticity prescription based on one seed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and remains in n-2e9e08198747 on the matched epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 observations per objective and ten-member batches. Direct N-halogen / O-halogen / O-O record counts are 489 / 145 / 114 in the current 4,350 products versus 1,042 / 278 / 273 in the Parent. Current leaders include N-F carboxamides, O-F and O-Cl groups, while conventional carbon-bound-fluorine cyclic amines, a tertiary aromatic carboxamide and halogen-free carbonyl leaders are counterexamples. The original component comparators have their own different flag counts and leaders; a lower aggregate flag count does not establish improved chemistry or score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within otherwise recognizable aromatic, carbonyl and amine frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide environment-aware local alternatives that preserve functional relationships supported by accepted task-local feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from direct N/O-halogen bonds, and assess N-O, N-N and sulfur groups in their actual environment. These are candidate chemical capabilities to test, not evidence for blanket filtering, a guaranteed score benefit or attribution to either changed component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and is re-observed under the current complete matched panel. Current products include 41 ring-triple-bond-bearing molecules and 61 with a ring carbon carrying two double bonds, versus Parent 17 and 42. Leaders include cyclic triple bonds, an enlarged aromatic-labelled N ring, small unsaturated rings and dense bridges. Ordinary azetidine and pyrrolidine aryl amines also score highly, and near-scoring alternatives lack some flagged bonds; small rings or fused systems are therefore not uniformly problematic.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid ring graph from a geometrically and synthetically credible ring construction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make local unsaturation, ring size, bridge connectivity and molecular state available to a task-agnostic assessment of proposed topology changes. Explore feasible alternatives preserving feedback-supported polar and aromatic relationships. Ring digits, aromatic labels, generic core counts and founder reachability supply no physical geometry evidence; neither a blanket ring ban nor component-specific causality follows.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This source gap was present in n-c55c3d520a2c and the reproduced n-62daf219c70a baseline, and is directly re-observed in n-2e9e08198747 at the matched current budget. The current evaluated stream spans one to 113 heavy atoms, with 299 products at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99, recency-only 105 and uniform-live-only 134. A terminal 51-heavy-atom coupled assembly scores 0.15510900536560693 below its 27-heavy-atom leader at 0.21177936240075523. Tiny products reach near-zero or zero scores in several objective sessions, but a small ether scores 0.5 in another, so the meaning of fragmentation depends on feedback. Compact conventional aryl amines remain strong counterexamples to a universal demand for larger structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of molecular-context loss and excessive elaboration while producing chemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted local feedback to preserve useful connected functional-group context through deletion, growth and replacement. Evaluate both simplifying and scaffold-changing alternatives without a universal minimum size or a preference for growth. These observations concern evaluated output only; they do not establish that useful unselected alternatives were unavailable, identify a retention or sampling mediator, or authorize rescue tuning of the ended fixed combination.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and persists across the current matched Search seeds and profile. All current task digest stereocentre incidences are 0.0, and no stereo markers occur in the read trajectories. RDKit identifies possible unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,446 of 4,350 current optimizer products versus 2,408 Parent products, including substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated carbocycles and bridged junctions. Available neutral amines are present despite zero charge incidence. No matched stereoisomer comparison or configurational-stability assessment is supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves many potentially stereogenic constitutions without an explicit stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical state when the generated constitution requires it, with explicit exceptions for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomerism separately. The evidence establishes incomplete specification, not an objective-specific preferred state, a measured score penalty or the contribution of a particular algorithm component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The conditional leading-family coverage gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and its n-62daf219c70a baseline and remains qualified rather than absolute in n-2e9e08198747. Current evaluated products have 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic nonempty Murcko cores, versus Parent 1,850 and 1,117; recency-only has 1,782 and 1,055, and uniform-live-only 2,060 and 1,403. Recurrent aromatic-carbonyl, cyclic-amine and fluorinated heterocyclic leaders coexist with real seed-family differences, tiny fragments, unusual aromatic-labelled rings and highly elaborated structures. These descriptors show perceived topology coverage, not retained founder atoms, chemical independence, feasibility or a mediator of endpoint differences.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct graph topologies do not translate into consistently demonstrated plausible alternatives to the leading chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Judge alternative scaffolds by preserved functional relationships, credible connectivity and actual accepted feedback, rather than string novelty, founder-union size or generic-core novelty alone. The generator already changes ring topology; the missing capability is reliable useful and plausible coverage. Preserve the original node/profile conditions and counterexamples when transferring this gap, and do not split the joint output into separate component value.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
